page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.16-256 is a memory-dense compute instance built on the 64-bit Arm architecture. The virtual machine delivers 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Ampere AmpereOne processor platform, operating at a sustained clock speed of 3.0 GHz. Unlike hyperthreaded architectures, the AmpereOne design provides a single execution thread per physical core, avoiding core-sharing contention and delivering consistent, predictable processing per vCPU.

The system is provisioned with 256 GB of main memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio that places it firmly within memory-optimized sizing profiles. There is no local NVMe or solid-state disk storage included with the configuration, which requires all persistence layers and operating system storage to rely on remote block volumes. The instance also excludes GPU hardware acceleration. From an infrastructure cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density per Arm core enables efficient consolidation of memory-bound applications without forcing the overprovisioning of compute resources.

Due to its arm64 instruction set architecture, operating software must support Arm compilation. The balance of 32 dedicated 3.0 GHz cores and 256 GB of memory makes this instance particularly well aligned with in-memory database deployments, distributed caching tiers like Redis or Memcached, data processing pipelines, ETL workloads, and large-footprint microservice clusters.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.16-256 is a memory-oriented virtual machine built on the Ampere AmpereOne arm64 platform. It features 32 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core, eliminating multi-tenant thread contention. The instance provides 256 GB of system memory, representing a high allocation ratio of 8 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is absent, with 0 GPUs, and no local disk storage is bundled, necessitating network-attached block volumes for persistent disk storage. One complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned by default. Given its large RAM-to-core ratio and consistent single-threaded compute profile, the instance provides cost-effective density for memory-demanding enterprise deployments, including in-memory databases, large-scale caching solutions, analytics platforms, and containerized microservice backends compatible with Arm.
